title: Familiar comfort with its cost discussable

captions.energy: Keeping convenience despite an increasing workload

meaning: Your domestic support preserves freedom when both can clarify familiar convenience’s cost instead of treating attachment as proof of its necessity.
text: Familiar domestic pleasure may seem especially necessary while other conditions remain unclear. The Moon in the physical position of Muladhara appears through actions based on an incomplete picture. The Devil in energy can retain convenience despite increasing work; the Devil in emotions experiences attachment to the familiar. A possible trap follows: checking an assumption of necessity becomes difficult because wanting to keep something pleasant starts determining which costs can be noticed and discussed together.

For example, keeping many ready entertainments at home feels convenient: games, subscriptions and spare devices. Any free evening seems likely to feel empty without them although actual use has not been discussed. Maintaining everything becomes burdensome. **Attachment to convenience does not remove permission to check how much it actually gives both.** Conversation about current use reveals pleasure alongside costs without declaring every favourite unnecessary or requiring immediate abandonment.

The difficulty is treating a question about cost as a threat to home itself and answering feared boredom with another purchase. Objects fill the unknown while freedom shrinks. Support grows when both can acknowledge desire without having to fulfil it at any price. The familiar remains a possibility when its place reflects present life rather than unchecked certainty that no peaceful evening is possible otherwise.
